newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby League - Super League changes rules to woo spectators.
newsitem.headline: Rugby League - Super League changes rules to woo spectators.

text.p: Media baron Rupert Murdoch's Super League have announced four rule changes in their drive to make rugby league more attractive to spectators when the breakaway competition starts in Australia next year.
The most radical of the changes announced on Sunday involves the restart after a try, with the scoring side now kicking off instead of the team who conceded the try.
All scrums will be set 20 metres in-field from touch instead of 10 and there will be no striking for the ball by defending players in play-the-balls.
There will also be an extra tackle added to the existing tackle count of six for players who pick up the ball from kicks by the opposing side instead of allowing it to roll into touch.

The Super League rule changes mean there are likely to be two sets of rules for the game in Australia after Murdoch's league scored a stunning legal win on Friday in its battle for control of the game with the Australian Rugby League, the sport's traditional rulers.
